chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
The Quru' (period of purity) is the time between the two menstruations.

key_terms.الْقُرْءُ: Quru': The period of purity between menstruations, used to determine legal status.

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of Quru' between two menstruations in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Isfabar, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) defines 'Quru'' as the period of purity between two menstruations, a definition central to Shia jurisprudence for determining the 'Iddah (waiting period) of divorce. This ruling distinguishes the Shia view from some Sunni schools by emphasizing the state of purity rather than just the menstrual cycle itself, thereby clarifying the legal status of women during this interval.
